commitments.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.summary: Security Incident reporting covers only incidents involving ePHI that the Business Associate or its Subcontractors handle for Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: Only Security Incidents involving ePHI created, received, maintained or transmitted for Covered Entity by Business Associate or its Subcontractors; incidents involving other data are outside the Section 4.2 duty.
commitments.deviation: The DPA defines a Personal Data Breach as a confirmed breach affecting Customer Personal Data and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The BAA instead uses the HIPAA Security Incident concept, which is not limited to confirmed events and includes attempts, limited to ePHI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may use or disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as this BAA permits.
commitments.scope: All PHI created, received, maintained or transmitted for Covered Entity under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions. The BAA limits use and disclosure by purpose (performance of the Underlying Agreements, legal requirement, or BAA permission), and the legal-requirement exception is wider than the DPA's instruction-only rule.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must apply the minimum-necessary standard to all uses and disclosures of PHI.
commitments.scope: All uses and disclosures of PHI.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements. Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and use the result only to provide and improve services under the Underlying Agreements; properly de-identified data falls outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: De-identified information is excluded from PHI and from the BAA, so incident, residency and deletion duties do not apply to it; use is limited to providing and improving services under the Underlying Agreements. Nothing in the BAA addresses AI model training (inference: it is not expressly permitted).
commitments.deviation: The DPA lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services, and bars foundation-model training on Customer Data. The BAA requires HIPAA safe-harbor de-identification and limits use to the services under the Underlying Agreements; it has no express foundation-model training bar and no 'secure' purpose.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: A limited data set is treated as PHI and is fully covered by the BAA.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) count as PHI for every BAA duty, including reporting, residency and return/destruction.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (Subpart C) for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to the Annex 2 security measures (AES-256, TLS 1.2+, MFA, etc.). The BAA instead requires compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule and lists no specific technical measures.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must not store or process PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, in any form, including as handled by Subcontractors (inference: through the Section 5.1 flow-down).
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data in the customer-selected hosting region, which may be outside the US. The BAA fixes storage and processing in the United States.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must not access PHI from outside the United States, which rules out offshore support access.
commitments.scope: All PHI; the access ban applies even for support, maintenance or security operations (inference from the absence of any exception).
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits access from outside the hosting region, including from Manila, Philippines. The BAA prohibits all access to PHI from outside the US and has no exception for support, maintenance or security operations.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 certification and does not mention SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and within 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach, a term the BAA takes from the HIPAA Rules (inference: the first day the Breach is known, or reasonably should have been known, to Business Associate)

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (per Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI as defined by the HIPAA Rules. Inference: a Breach of ePHI is also a Security Incident under 4.2, and the BAA has no precedence clause, so the shorter 5-business-day period in 4.2 would also apply.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach. The BAA allows 10 calendar days, which is longer, but runs from Discovery (not confirmation) and is expressed in calendar days.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becomes aware of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (per Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity (Section 1.2). Awareness is the Business Associate's own; the BAA does not say whether Subcontractor awareness counts.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 72 hours from ExampleCo's confirmation of a breach. The BAA gives 5 business days from awareness (not confirmation) and covers all Security Incidents, not only confirmed breaches, so the trigger is earlier but the period is longer.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: This section is the standing notice for unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-ins, and no further report is required for them.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts from the definition of Personal Data Breach, so no notice is owed. The BAA treats them as Security Incidents but deems this section to be the notice.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must report any use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becomes aware of the unpermitted use or disclosure

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (per Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA, whether or not it amounts to a Breach or Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA only requires notice of confirmed Personal Data Breaches.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: All Section 4 reports must be written and sent to the Privacy Office with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: Breach, Security Incident and unpermitted use or disclosure reports under Section 4.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the administration console, or else to the account owner. The BAA fixes two named email addresses and requires a written report with a copy to a second office.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, the affected individuals, the PHI involved, the Breach and Discovery dates, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (per Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches only, not Security Incident or unpermitted use reports.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, categories of data and measures taken or proposed. The BAA requires more specific content (identity of each individual, dates) but contains no express duty to supply further information as it becomes available.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and media about a Breach it or its Subcontractors caused.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors; the clause covers notification costs only (individuals, regulators, media).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA has no cost reimbursement term and states that breach notification is not an acknowledgment of fault.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must bind every Subcontractor that handles PHI in writing to the same restrictions and conditions as the BAA.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103 that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on Business Associate's behalf.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessors' performance and provides general authorization with 30 days' notice and an objection right (5.1-5.4). The BAA requires only written flow-down of the same terms and has no notice, objection or list-publication terms.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days after its request.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary to determine HIPAA compliance.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives audit rights only to Customer, satisfied by its reports, with one on-site audit if a supervisory authority requires it. The BAA gives the HHS Secretary access to books and records with no notice period or frequency limit, and gives Covered Entity no audit right of its own.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: Business Associate must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days after termination of the Underlying Agreements.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.scope: All PHI, with no stated separate backup period.
commitments.deviation: The DPA deletes within 90 days after termination or expiry, with backups overwritten within a further 35 days, and offers written deletion certification on request. The BAA requires return or destruction within 30 days, includes a return option, sets no backup period and has no certification term.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If return or destruction of PHI is not feasible, Business Associate must keep applying the BAA's protections to that PHI for as long as it holds it.

deadline.anchor: for as long as Business Associate retains the PHI

commitments.scope: PHI for which return or destruction is infeasible.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no infeasibility exception. It requires deletion, with backups overwritten in the ordinary course.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA overrides the Subscription Agreement and any Vendor or Affiliate data processing terms, policies or online terms.
commitments.scope: Applies to all VDPA duties. It matters most for incident notice, because the 24-hour period in 6.1 displaces a longer period in any Vendor or Affiliate terms such as a standard DPA. Type chosen as the duty most affected (inference).
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA controls over the Agreement only as to processing of Customer Personal Data. This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and also over Vendor's and its Affiliates' own DPA, policies and online terms, with no limit to personal data.

commitments.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: All data from Retailer, its employees or customers, or collected from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and derived data, is protected Retailer Data.
commitments.scope: Defines the data covered by every duty in the VDPA. It is not limited to personal data and includes derived data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA applies only to Customer Personal Data. This VDPA covers all data, including telemetry and derived data, whether or not personal.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA treats the Agreement, the DPA and the customer's configuration of the Services as documented instructions. This VDPA requires Retailer's written instructions and limits processing to providing the Services.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model unless the model is used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.scope: Any machine learning model, and all Retailer Data including derived data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA bars only training or fine-tuning of foundation models made available to other customers, and lets ExampleCo use Usage Data to improve the Services (8.2). This VDPA bars training or improving any ML model that is not Retailer-only. Because Retailer Data includes derived data, the baseline Usage Data right appears not to apply (inference).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Vendor must store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Storage of Retailer Data. The clause does not address access from other locations, and the VDPA has no separate offshore-access term.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA stores data in the customer-selected hosting region. This VDPA fixes the locations to the US or Canada. The baseline 6.2 right to access data from outside the region, including Manila, has no counterpart here. Whether such access is allowed is not stated (inference).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards that meet or exceed CIS Critical Security Controls Implementation Group 2.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA commits to the Annex 2 measures, which Vendor may update if overall security is not materially reduced. This VDPA sets an external benchmark (CIS IG2) and has no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Annex 2 specifies AES-256 and TLS 1.2 or higher. This VDPA says only 'industry-standard'. It has no multi-factor authentication or business continuity/disaster recovery term.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year and provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request.
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report on the Services every year and give it to Retailer within 15 days of a request.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's request for the SOC 2 Type II report

secondary_deadline.anchor: annual SOC 2 Type II report cycle

commitments.scope: SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 and gives access through the Trust Center under NDA terms (9.1). This VDPA requires only SOC 2 Type II, delivered directly within 15 days of request. It has no ISO 27001 requirement and no Trust Center NDA condition.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Only Subprocessors listed in Appendix B may process Retailer Data unless Retailer gives prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Subprocessor includes any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, processing Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf (2.4).
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA gives general authorization to engage Subprocessors. This VDPA requires prior written consent for any Subprocessor not in Appendix B, and Affiliates count as Subprocessors.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: Vendor must request Retailer's written consent for a new Subprocessor at least 30 days before it starts processing, and silence is not consent.

deadline.anchor: new Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.scope: Any new Subprocessor, including Vendor Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA gives 30 days' notice by Trust Center update and email, with a 15-day objection right and termination remedy (5.3). This VDPA requires a written consent request with an affirmative approval requirement. It has no urgent-replacement exception (5.4).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA, and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor must flow down obligations at least as protective as the VDPA to each Subprocessor in writing and remains liable for their acts and omissions.
commitments.scope: Each Subprocessor, including Vendor Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA states only that ExampleCo remains responsible for Subprocessors' performance. This VDPA adds a written flow-down duty and liability for acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Hosting | United States
commitments.summary: AWS is an approved Subprocessor for hosting in the United States.
commitments.scope: Hosting; location United States.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA publishes its Subprocessor list on the Trust Center and allows additions on notice. This VDPA fixes an approved list in Appendix B.

commitments.quote: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | United States
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. is an approved Subprocessor for support ticketing in the United States.
commitments.scope: Support ticketing; location United States.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA publishes its Subprocessor list on the Trust Center and allows additions on notice. This VDPA fixes an approved list in Appendix B.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States
commitments.summary: Amendment No. 1 (September 8, 2025) approves Vendor Affiliate ExampleCo, Inc. as a Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features in the United States.
commitments.scope: Limited to platform hosting and AI features for the Services, in the United States. Section 3.2 still restricts ML training on Retailer Data, and section 1.1 means ExampleCo's standard DPA terms do not override the VDPA.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA would allow this on general authorization with 30 days' notice. Here the approval is specific and limited by purpose and location, and the VDPA terms govern over ExampleCo's standard DPA (1.1).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and within 24 hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor becomes aware of the Data Incident (Vendor's own awareness, of an actual or reasonably suspected incident, not confirmation)

commitments.scope: Data Incident means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA allows 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. This VDPA allows 24 hours from awareness and covers suspected incidents and data held by Subprocessors. Under 1.1 this period displaces any longer period in Vendor or Affiliate terms.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182. Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both email and telephone to Retailer Security Operations, and notice to account or procurement contacts does not count.
commitments.scope: Notices under 6.1.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA sends notice to the security contact set in the admin console, or else the account owner. This VDPA names fixed contacts, requires both email and phone, and rejects account or procurement contacts.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.summary: The incident notice must describe the incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps taken.
commitments.scope: Content of Data Incident notices.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA requires nature, data categories and measures, 'to the extent then known'. This VDPA drops that qualifier, requires identifying the Subprocessor involved, and refers to the actual Retailer Data involved.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: Vendor must supplement the incident notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.scope: Updates to Data Incident notices.
commitments.deviation: Substantially similar to the baseline duty to provide further information as it becomes available, with no different timing.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not tell Retailer's customers or any third party about a Data Incident without Retailer's prior written approval, unless the law requires it.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents involving Retailer Data; exception for legally required disclosures.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation of a Data Incident.
commitments.scope: Retailer's investigation of Data Incidents.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors
commitments.summary: Vendor must bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent Vendor or its Subprocessors caused it.
commitments.scope: Reasonable Data Incident costs, to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors, including Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The baseline DPA says only that its breach response is not an admission of fault (7.4) and has no cost allocation.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends.

deadline.anchor: Subscription Agreement ends

commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data. No backup overwrite extension is stated.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA allows 90 days plus 35 days for backups and covers only Customer Personal Data. This VDPA allows 30 days, covers all Retailer Data, and states no backup extension.

commitments.quote: and confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.
commitments.summary: Vendor must confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.

deadline.anchor: Subscription Agreement ends (inference: the confirmation falls in the same sentence as the 30-day deletion period)

commitments.scope: Written confirmation of deletion of all Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA provides written certification only on the customer's request. This VDPA requires written confirmation without a request.

commitments.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice, and within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident.
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's VDPA compliance once per calendar year on 30 days' notice, and also within 10 days after notice following a Data Incident.

deadline.anchor: calendar year (one audit per year on 30 days' notice)

secondary_deadline.anchor: Retailer's notice of an audit following a Data Incident

commitments.scope: Vendor's compliance with the whole VDPA.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA limits audits to reliance on SOC 2 and pen-test reports, with one on-site audit per 12 months only where a supervisory authority requires it, on 60 days' notice, at the customer's expense. This VDPA gives an unconditional annual audit on 30 days' notice plus a post-incident audit within 10 days, and does not say who bears the cost.

commitments.quote: This VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.summary: The VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.scope: All VDPA duties. Type chosen as the closest fit.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: A change of control of Vendor, by merger, acquisition or otherwise, does not terminate or modify this VDPA. Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.summary: A change of control of Vendor does not end or change the VDPA, and an acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data without Retailer's written agreement.
commitments.scope: Change of control of Vendor and all Retailer Data. Type chosen as the closest fit.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides any conflicting term in the Agreement, order forms, and any Supplier DPA or policy.
commitments.scope: All Supplier documents, including any data processing addendum such as ExampleCo's standard DPA.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA controls over the Agreement as to Customer Personal Data; here the Bank's Addendum controls over the Agreement and over any Supplier DPA.

commitments.quote: Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Terms that live on Supplier websites or trust sites do not bind the Bank or change the Addendum.
commitments.scope: Supplier website and Trust Center terms, such as the Trust Center subprocessor list and notice mechanics in the baseline.
commitments.deviation: The baseline DPA relies on the Trust Center for subprocessor lists, notices, and reports; here such site-based terms are non-binding on the Bank.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Protected Bank Data covers all data in any form including metadata, logs, derived data, model outputs, and aggregated or de-identified data.
commitments.scope: All data handled by Supplier or any Subcontractor in connection with the Agreement, including aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized and tokenized derivatives.
commitments.deviation: The baseline covers only Personal Data within Customer Data and treats de-identified Usage Data as outside scope; here all data, including metadata and de-identified or derived data, is protected.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a written security program aligned to NIST CSF and the FFIEC handbook.
commitments.deviation: The baseline commits to the Annex 2 measures without naming external frameworks; here a written program consistent with NIST CSF and the FFIEC handbook is required.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Bank Data must be encrypted at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: Bank Data as broadly defined.
commitments.deviation: Same encryption standards as Annex 2 (which also allows no stronger standard), but applies to the broader Bank Data definition.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Multi-factor authentication is required for all remote access to systems handling Bank Data.
commitments.scope: Remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline requires MFA for production system access; here MFA is required for all remote access to systems handling Bank Data.
